quote: (Treten da Gruppen auf? Infinitesimale Transfor- mation!)
topic: A list of research notes: treating certain functions by analogy with Eisenstein's work on the p-function via infinite products, addition theorems for p and σ, turning covariant criteria into invariant ones, decomposition conditions for binary forms in several variables, vanishing of transvectants, Klein's topic of a typical representation of the Kummer surface, and termination of chains of transvection processes.

triage.modern_statement: The note is too fragmentary to pin down. It is a marginal aside in a list of research topics, and it is unclear which item it belongs to. The most plausible reading, given the neighbouring items (turning covariant criteria into invariant ones, decomposition conditions for binary forms, vanishing of transvectants, and whether chains of transvection steps terminate), is this: can the invariance conditions for binary forms be described through a continuous (Lie) transformation group, replacing the group condition with its infinitesimal (Lie-algebra) version, i.e. linear differential operators that the invariants must satisfy? If so, it is a methodological reminder to use Lie's infinitesimal method, not a well-defined open problem.
triage.answered_by: There is no specific answer, because no specific question can be identified. The general idea, studying invariants of binary forms through infinitesimal generators of the transformation group, was standard in Lie's and Hilbert's time and became the infinitesimal method of classical invariant theory. Hilbert's own early invariant-theory work derived invariant criteria for special binary forms from differential equations. An English translation of those papers appears in Ackerman and Hermann (eds.), Lie Groups: History, Frontiers and Applications vol. 8, 1978.

evidence.claim: Lie's infinitesimal approach to invariance is a standard part of classical invariant theory. It replaces complicated group conditions with their infinitesimal (Lie-algebra) versions, which linearizes the analysis, and the textbook covers it for binary forms.

Hilbert's invariant-theory papers include work on invariant properties and criteria for special binary forms derived from algebraic differential equations, which is the area of the neighbouring notebook items. They were translated in the Lie Groups: History, Frontiers and Applications series, vol. 8.
